reasoning: Both attempts handle instance reduction, parent-last creation and frame budgeting equally well, and both pass all checks. B reserves every saved cell before loading starts, which meets the core requirement of criterion 4. A reserves cells lazily, so placements made during a load can permanently skip saved blocks. A handles unloading better by holding the slot and cells until the parts are gone, while B has a brief, documented overlap. On balance, B's guard on the load path matters more, so B wins.

criteria.note: Owner/PlacedAt value objects replaced by a `PlacedAt` attribute and the `plot.blocks` table, so each block is one part; placed time is kept for saved and new blocks.
`templates[blockType]:Clone()` gets its CFrame and attribute set, then `part.Parent = plot.folder` comes last.
A Heartbeat `runJobs` advances load and unload jobs under a shared FRAME_BUDGET of 4 ms and MAX_BLOCKS_PER_FRAME of 500; unloading resumes from a `next` cursor.

`stepLoad` sets `occupied[cell]` only as each block is created, so cells aren't reserved before the first yield and placements during a load can take saved cells; leaving mid-load is handled well (isClosed, unload job, slot held until the plot is empty).
Removal requires `plots[player].blocks[block]` plus the reach check and frees the stored cell; placement validation is unchanged.
Says builds appear over about 0.7–3 s as a rough estimate, includes a 'Not yet verified' section, and lists what players will notice, including the skipped-block behaviour.

criteria.note: Typed Plot/Job unions and all checks pass; the slot-wait BindableEvent is solid, but the lazy reservation is a correctness gap.
`blocks[part] = {OwnerId, PlacedAt, Cell, Plot}` table and no value children; adds only one Chunk folder per 100 blocks.
`createBlock` returns an unparented part; saved blocks go under a detached `Chunk` folder that is parented once.
`runJobs` does work under a 4 ms / 500-block budget and calls `task.wait()` between frames; unloading destroys chunks over several frames.

`reserveSavedBlocks` marks every cell occupied before the job is queued, and leaving mid-load frees pending cells and stops the job; but cells and slot are freed before old parts are destroyed, which allows a brief, documented overlap on unload.
Removal checks `block.OwnerId ~= player.UserId` plus reach and frees `block.Cell`; placement validation is unchanged.
Before/after table is clearly marked 'expected, not measured', gives about 1–2 s per full build, and lists the progressive appearance, unload overlap and Chunk folders.
